title: Hybrid allowlist safekeeper for route-adaptive batching & KV-prefetch
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a hybrid 'allowlist safekeeper' component that produces per-route and per-customer recommendations for batching and KV-prefetch policies, evaluates safety via dry-run simulation, and applies config changes via a staged canary with automated rollback triggers. The goal is to safely capture cost upside from batching/prefetch without degrading latency or model quality for high-tier customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) System generates per-route recommendations (batch_size_hint, prefetch_enabled, prefetch_ttl, allowlist/denylist) and exposes them in the console for review; 2) Dry-run simulator can replay 7 days of traffic for a selected route and output cost delta, tail-latency delta, and quality regressions (measured by NLL/heuristic); 3) Staged apply supports: sandbox -> 1% canary -> 10% canary -> full rollout; 4) Automated rollback triggers on: >5% tail-latency regression, >3% quality drop on eval suite, or >20% unexpected cost increase vs simulated; 5) Rollout audits are logged to customer audit trail and changelog entries link to the originating recommendation; 6) Unit and e2e tests cover simulation, policy engine, and rollback hooks.
implementation_notes:
- Policy model: combine deterministic segmentation (customer tier, route, SLA) with a lightweight ML scorer that predicts risk of quality regression based on prompt statistics and recent eval signals.
- Recommendation output schema: {route, customer_segment, recommended_batch_size, prefetch: {enabled, ttl_ms}, allowlist_rules, denylist_rules, confidence_score, simulated_metrics}.
- Dry-run: replay requests against a shadow runtime with KV cache/prefetch enabled and record end-to-end timing and token counts; costs are estimated using current pricing model.
- Apply: use existing ruleforge infra to stage rules with a 'safekeeper' flag; integrations with rollout service for percent-based traffic splits.
- Rollback: implement automated policy that flips safekeeper->disabled and marks the recommendation as 'failed' with reason tags; also create a follow-up incident ticket template for manual investigation.
- Telemetry: augment per-route telemetry with predicted vs observed metrics to improve the scorer over time.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime-optimize.experimental.allowlist_safekeeper; 2) Internal sandbox validation using synthetic traffic and two low-risk beta customers; 3) 1% canary across selected routes (runtime-1 CPU/GPU pools) for 48 hours; 4) If stable, expand to 10% for 72 hours; 5) Full rollout with daily checks for first 7 days; 6) Post-rollout A/B quality evaluation on historical eval set and customer ping checks.
monitoring_signals: - 50/95/99th tail latency for affected routes; - tokens/sec and average tokens per request; - model output quality heuristics (BLEU/NLL proxies where applicable); - per-customer error rates and 5-minute failure spikes; - cost per-token and projected monthly cost delta; - rollout traffic fraction and canary health metrics.
rollback_playbook:
- Trigger: automated threshold breach or manual abort.
- Steps: 1) Flip recommendation state to 'disabled' and publish an emergency policy change that disables prefetch/batch changes for the affected routes; 2) Notify oncall + PM + review board via Slack alert channel #runtime-ops; 3) Open incident with auto-populated diagnostics (links to dry-run, observed-vs-expected graphs, last 100 requests sampled); 4) If rollback fails to recover within 15 minutes, escalate to SRE for routing-level mitigation (reroute to previous runtime variant); 5) Post-incident retro and update allowlist/denylist logic as needed.
risk_tradeoffs:
- Aggressiveness vs safety: higher batch sizes yield better cost per token but increase tail latency risk; using a conservative confidence threshold reduces cost upside but improves safety.
- Complexity vs operability: adding ML scorer increases precision but requires retraining and monitoring; initial launch will use deterministic heuristics plus simple linear risk model.
- Per-customer fairness: must ensure lower-tier customers cannot be silently degraded; proposals include opt-out, explicit allowlist for high-tier, and mandatory audit trail for any change that impacts enterprise customers.
decision_log: - 2026-02-14: Chose hybrid approach (deterministic segmentation + scorer) after design review: avoids cold-start for rare routes. - 2026-02-20: Set rollback thresholds (latency 5%, quality 3%) after SRE cost-of-false-positive analysis. - 2026-02-25: Agreed to require explicit audit tags for enterprise-tier changes and customer notification when prefetch is enabled.
